gameVerifiedNote: Static evidence only: interop metadata from the Forge-MapEditor-QA profile and dump.cs of the same build. No hook was installed and nothing was executed, so the audit reads the compiled plugin's patch targets, postfix shapes, read set and declared write entries and never claims native call timing; a declared write entry says which member the plugin calls, not that the call changed anything in a running game.

postfixVocabulary.instanceParameter: the Harmony `__instance` parameter the postfix takes, named exactly as the patched type; null when the postfix takes no instance
postfixVocabulary.arguments: the postfix parameters that follow the instance, each with the exact interop type the postfix declares
postfixVocabulary.reads: exactly those parameters whose value the postfix body loads with ldarg/ldarga; an empty list means the callback's own arguments are never consulted and the fact comes from a re-read
postfixVocabulary.guard: the MapPluginSession method the postfix gates its work with: Guard for the player readbacks, GuardMapObjects for the map-object and expedition readbacks

writeVocabulary.writes: the game members the compiled plugin calls to carry an action out: the door and terminal entries of this provider's map-object half, and the player health receiver's one write entry. Each row names one member and is resolved against the interop assemblies exactly as a readback row is; each is documented by its own member row in the evidence document that owns its domain (evidence/door-terminal-hooks.json for the door and terminal entries, evidence/player-health.json for the player health entry), which carries the build's RVA (or field offset) and the bytes at it. The audit compares this set to the plugin's non-getter game calls both ways: a non-getter call no row declares fails, and a declared entry the plugin no longer calls fails.
writeVocabulary.notAWrite: `LG_SecurityDoor.AttemptDamage` is deliberately absent: on this build its address holds the folded empty body (`ret 0`), so it carries no implementation and invoking it could only fake a damage. It is recorded as a refusal in evidence/door-terminal-hooks.json instead of being declared here.

hooks.name: OnDoorState
hooks.readback: the door the lock component belongs to, re-read through the component's own m_door after the body; the callback's pDoorState argument is not a fact source

hooks.name: OnExpeditionEnded
hooks.readback: the game's own end state of the expedition that just ended, taken from the callback's argument and published as the trigger's `outcome`; nothing is re-read, because the game states the outcome here, and deriving it from a game state name, a player count or a teardown order would be a second, weaker answer

hooks.name: OnPlayerDespawned
hooks.readback: retire lives whose agent is no longer in PlayerAgentsInLevel or no longer linked to its player

hooks.name: OnPlayerSpawned
hooks.readback: PlayerAgentsInLevel and each agent's linked SNet_Player after an agent was spawned for a player

hooks.name: OnStateChange
hooks.readback: the terminal's own CurrentStateName and, while a player is at it, the interaction source the session actor is resolved from; oldState/newState are not fact sources

readbacks.note: declared on the agent base type; the PlayerAgent call site binds to that one declaration
the rundown block the process loaded; MTFO 4.6.3 reads the same member to select the parsed rundown table
an observation fact and the way a native callback's id is turned back into a terminal; it is never part of an address

the terminal's own command interpreter, read through the interop property of its `m_command` field (0xB0). The command action asks that interpreter to parse the line, so a line the terminal does not know can never become a command.

the manager the static command entry belongs to, read through the interop property of its static `Current` field (0x0); the command action refuses when it reads nothing, because the entry's own authoritative action is an instance field of it
the only entry point to the level's zone list; whether it is already assigned when a hook first runs is not verified in game.

the door's own statement whether it may be interacted with right now; the open action refuses on it rather than asking a door that says no. Its own body address is shared with a compiler-generated lambda of the same type, which the member row in evidence/door-terminal-hooks.json records.
the game's own door type; `Bulkhead` is how a layer transition door is told from a zone entrance

the zone's own terminal list: it is both the zone a terminal belongs to and the placement index that names it inside that zone, so the two can never disagree. Whether its order equals the zone's TerminalPlacements order is not verified in game.
the zone's own entrance gate; whether it is the gate a player enters the zone through is not verified in game, and neither is whether the start zone has none.
whether the prompt a no-key lock carries holds text; the first `Localization.` member this module reads, and the action refuses an empty prompt instead of sending one
the active expedition as a value type; the tier and the index are read off it, never off the game's own key string
the game's own key for the same expedition (`Local_31_TierA_0`); written to the level-identity record, never compared

readbacks.privacy: Steam64 account ID on real players: private dictionary key only; never in entity IDs, logs, errors, observers or evidence

the door's own interaction entry and the only member that opens or closes a security door.
